# CLI reference

Every verb and flag of the jint command, generated from the CLI.

<!-- generated:reference — do not edit. Regenerate with `bun run schema`. -->

## Verbs

The first operand is the verb. There is no default verb.

| Verb         | Example                                             | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `run`        | `jint run src/`                                     | classify an input: paths, the str/paths stdin nouns, or the discovered config; needs OPENAI_API_KEY (or JINT_API_URL, with JINT_API_KEY unless the server is local) in the environment                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `serve`      | `jint serve`                                        | the run UI over the store's newest run - hold, Ctrl+C to exit; binds loopback only (override: JINT_UI_HOST - a non-loopback host is your trust decision, a port in it is rejected); honors JINT_UI_PORT                                                                                                                                                             |
| `capture`    | `jint capture doc.md`                               | print extraction - grammar, kind, span, name - with the classifier unplugged; loads the config like run (its input when no target, its rules.exclude always); an explicit FILE target bypasses the config's rules scope (a dir target never does) - capture prints structure, no classifier, while run's file operand evaluates the config scope for unscoped rules |
| `reclassify` | `jint reclassify <run-id> src/a.ts --rule <name> -` | classify one rule at one input of a recorded run again and file it under that run as its next #N, where the run UI shows it at once; with a trailing - a JSON edit ({instructions, criteria, code}, only what changed) is read from stdin, without it the original question is asked again; needs the endpoint key like run                                         |
| `skills`     | `jint skills export .claude/skills`                 | write the agent skills that ship with jint (jint-follow, jint-author, jint-propose) into a directory, one folder per skill, replacing files that exist                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

## Flags

| Flag            | Argument     | Verbs   | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------- | ------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--language`    | `<id>`       | all     | tree-sitter grammar for piped-stdin/extensionless sources; valid ids: typescript, tsx, python, markdown, php, go, cpp, c, bash, css, json, toml, yaml (derived from the grammar map). Without a resolvable language, inventory-scoped rules fail WALK_FAILED in-band and unit-scoped rules still classify |
| `--config`      | `<path>`     | all     | config file (auto-discovered: jint.config.ts or jint.config.json; JSON autocomplete via the "$schema" key)                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--exclude`     | `<glob>`     | all     | input exclusion, on top of config (repeatable)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--disable`     | `<name>`     | all     | rule removal by name, on top of config (repeatable)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--rule`        | `<name>`     | all     | run: ONLY these rules (repeatable; overrides --disable). capture: ONE name - preview the population it will judge, marked with * (nothing is classified). reclassify: ONE name - the rule to reclassify (required)                                                                                        |
| `--concurrency` | `<n>`        | all     | max in-flight classifier calls, run-wide (default 16, max 64; overrides the config key of the same name)                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--timeout`     | `<secs>`     | all     | per-call classifier timeout in seconds, retries included (default 30; each attempt gets a third of it; a hung call becomes a per-element PROVIDER_TIMEOUT failure)                                                                                                                                        |
| `--queries`     | `<file.scm>` | capture | capture only: the .scm file that drives extraction, replacing the grammar's own queries.scm                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--grammar`     | `<dir>`      | capture | capture only: a grammar dir (<id>.wasm + extensions.json [+ queries.scm]) registered custom for this call                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--json`        |              | all     | machine report (byte-identical to the run's report.json) instead of raw finding lines                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--dry-run`     |              | all     | print the rule set that WOULD run (config resolved, disable/only applied) and exit 0 - zero input walks, zero classifier calls                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--unscoped`    |              | run     | run: measure named files and a path list as given - the config's rules scope (rules.include/exclude) is not applied; a rule's own include/exclude still is                                                                                                                                                |
| `--no-cache`    |              | run     | run: ask every question instead of serving stored answers (the answer cache is $JINT_CACHE_DIR, else ~/.jint/cache)                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--no-header`   |              | run     | run: do not print the rules and scope header on stderr (the rules stay in the report's rules)                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--debug`       |              | all     | structured debug logs on stderr                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--help`, `-h`  |              | all     | this help                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--version`     |              | all     | print the version                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
